candidate.answerReason: The four separate slabs have total surface area 12 square feet. Their three glued interfaces have combined area 1/2 square foot, removing twice that area and leaving 11 square feet.

methods.label: Subtract the glued faces
methods.explanation:
It is easier to find the surface areas of the four separate pieces first, then remove the surfaces hidden by glue.

The cube has side length \(1\) foot. Each piece is therefore a rectangular slab with a \(1\)-by-\(1\) top and bottom. Let \(a,b,c,d\) be the heights of pieces \(A,B,C,D\), respectively. The cuts give
\[
a=\frac12,\qquad b=\frac13,\qquad c=\frac1{17},
\]
and
\[
d=1-\frac12-\frac13-\frac1{17}
=\frac{11}{102}.
\]
All four heights are positive and add to \(1\).

A separate slab of height \(t\) has two square faces of area \(1\) each and four rectangular faces of area \(t\) each. Thus the total surface area before gluing is
\[
4\cdot2+4(a+b+c+d)=8+4=12.
\]
In the displayed arrangement, the bottoms are aligned and each join has width \(1\). Its height is the height of the shorter neighboring slab. Since \(c<b<a\) and \(d<a\), the glued areas at the joins \(C\)-\(B\), \(B\)-\(A\), and \(A\)-\(D\) are \(c,b,d\), respectively. Their sum is
\[
c+b+d=1-a=\frac12.
\]
Each glued patch was counted twice in the separate surface areas, once on each neighboring piece. Both copies become internal, so the exposed surface area is
\[
12-2\left(\frac12\right)=\boxed{11}
\]
square feet, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses rectangular-prism surface areas, elementary fraction arithmetic, and subtraction of glued rectangles.

methods.label: Group the exposed faces by direction
methods.explanation:
Group the exposed faces into horizontal faces, the front and back, and the vertical ends and steps. This keeps every part of the surface accounted for.

The original cube has side length \(1\) foot, so every slab has a \(1\)-by-\(1\) horizontal footprint. Write \(a,b,c,d\) for the heights of \(A,B,C,D\). Then
\[
a=\frac12,\quad b=\frac13,\quad c=\frac1{17},
\]
\[
d=1-\frac12-\frac13-\frac1{17}
=\frac{11}{102}.
\]
In particular, \(a+b+c+d=1\), \(c<b<a\), and \(0<d<a\).

Each slab's entire top and bottom remain exposed because the slabs are joined along vertical end faces. These eight unit squares contribute \(8\) square feet.

At the front, the four rectangular portions each have length \(1\), so their total area is \(a+b+c+d=1\). The back contributes another \(1\), giving \(2\) square feet together.

The remaining faces are the two ends and the three vertical steps. Reading from \(C\) through \(B,A,D\), their heights are
\[
c,\quad b-c,\quad a-b,\quad a-d,\quad d.
\]
Each has width \(1\), so their combined area is
\[
\begin{aligned}
c+(b-c)+(a-b)+(a-d)+d
&=2a\\
&=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
These groups cover all exposed faces, without counting any glued patch. The total surface area is therefore
\[
8+2+1=\boxed{11}
\]
square feet, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method adds rectangular surface portions and uses elementary cancellation of slab-height differences.

review.mathematicalCheck: The slab heights are 1/2, 1/3, 1/17, and 11/102, summing to 1. The figure supports aligned bottoms and unit-width joins. Separate surface areas total 12; glued areas total 1/17 + 1/3 + 11/102 = 1/2, leaving 12 − 2(1/2) = 11. Independently, exposed horizontal faces contribute 8, front and back contribute 2, and ends and steps contribute 2a = 1.
